title: MOASYS-Vault — warnings.json (and validation-warnings.json, plex-warnings.json, plex-log-warnings.json)
description: The on-disk shape for every warnings file the scanner writes. Warnings are grouped by the top-level library folder they concern — a show, movie, artist, or author — because that is the unit of work: one show is one entry, however many checks fired on it. Each row's `path` is relative to its folder's `path`, and is absent when the warning is about the folder itself. A row carries only what locates and states the problem: the remedy for a warning type is identical on every row of that type, so its home is the warning tables in docs/OUTPUT.md rather than the file. `folders` is sorted alphabetically by path, so a diff between runs shows what actually changed. The validation pass uses the same shape under output/<drive>/<type>/validation-warnings.json, and the Plex commands under plex-warnings.json (`npm run plex:check`) and plex-log-warnings.json (`npm run plex:logs`) — plus copies under unfiltered/ when run with --no-ignore. The merged view produced by `npm run report` is a superset; see all-warnings.json.

generated.description: ISO 8601 UTC timestamp of when the file was written.

count.description: Total warnings collected. Equals the sum of every folder's `count`. Excludes warnings silenced by ignored/<drive>/<type>.yaml.

by_type.description: How many rows each warning type produced, ordered worst first. Keys are 'warn_*' identifiers matching toggles in rules/<type>.yaml under `checks`; the exceptions are filesystem-level failures that aren't user-toggleable, e.g. permission_denied. Sparse — only types that fired appear.

folders.description: One entry per top-level library folder with at least one warning, sorted alphabetically by `path`.

WarningFolder.description: Every warning on one top-level library folder. Deliberately flat: a season, album, or book is a relative `path` on a row, never a nested entry.

path.description: Library-relative path of the folder, forward-slash-normalized — the prefix every row hangs off, e.g. `SD/Good Eats (1999)`. Empty only for a warning at the library root of a library with no categories. The last segment is the name an ignore-list entry uses; a path with no `/` is either a category folder (silenced under `folders:`) or, in a library with no `categories`, the top-level name itself.

count.description: Number of rows on this folder. Equals `rows.length`.

rows.description: The warnings on this folder, sorted by canonical relative path (folder-level rows first), then type, then issue. Canonical, so a scan's `Season 03` sits next to a TMDB pass's `Season 3`.

type.description: Stable warning identifier, e.g. `warn_quality_mismatch` — the key into the file's `by_type`, the toggle name under `checks` in rules/<type>.yaml, and the row in the docs/OUTPUT.md warning table that gives the remedy.

path.description: Location relative to the folder's `path`, forward-slash-normalized — e.g. `Season 09` under `SD/Good Eats (1999)`. ABSENT means the warning is about the folder itself.

issue.description: Human-readable statement of the problem — the facts that differ row to row. The remedy is in the docs/OUTPUT.md warning table under this row's `type`.

extension.description: Optional file extension. Only present for non-primary file warnings (warn_non_primary).
